checks.name: Companion radius
checks.detail: planet-sized

checks.detail: a main-sequence dwarf (Teff 3376 K)

checks.detail: Gaia RUWE 7.03 > 1.4: the astrometry doesn't fit a single star (an unresolved companion is likely)
checks.value: Gaia DR3 RUWE 7.03, IPD harmonic 0.018, multi-peak 0% · ExoFOP companions 0

checks.name: Already catalogued
checks.detail: not a TOI, CTOI, known planet or catalogued binary at this period
checks.value: checked: TOIs, CTOIs, confirmed planets, TESS EB catalog, AAVSO VSX, Gaia DR3 eclipsing binaries and orbits

checks.name: Period recovery
checks.detail: no repeat of the transit in 344 days of TESS data (nothing of its depth above 7.0σ); most probable P ≈ 648 d (68%: 278-1310 d), from the periods the data allow and the transit probability; a second transit fixes it: the next TESS sectors of the star, or ground photometry
checks.value: 16 sectors scanned (344 d) · ZTF has too few points on the star · 22% of 8.04-2000 d allowed by the TESS coverage

checks.name: Individual transits
checks.detail: one transit: the period is unknown
checks.value: BTJD 1635.16: vetting SNR 5.6, 25.3 ppt (the search's SNR was 14.8: a different detrending, binning and noise estimate)

checks.name: Event consistency
checks.detail: compares transits with each other: a periodic signal only

checks.name: Signal uniqueness (single event)
checks.detail: a brightening at BTJD 1649.74 is also above the false-alarm threshold: the systematics make events this size in both directions
checks.value: the dip 7.4σ white, 6.1σ red (F_red 1.22 from 4109 box positions over 342 d); threshold 4.6σ (noise reaches it anywhere in that much data 1% of the time); strongest brightening 8.2σ red at BTJD 1649.74

checks.name: SNR growth
checks.detail: how the SNR builds over transits: a periodic signal only

checks.name: Period consistency
checks.detail: one transit: there's no period to check (the alias and shape checks bound it instead)

checks.name: Alias periods
checks.detail: periods under 8.0 d would have shown a second transit in the data around the dip; on this star a 2.00 h transit needs P ≳ 5.3 d (central, circular orbit)

checks.name: Detrending sensitivity
checks.detail: survives 4 detrendings (two methods, transits masked) with the depth within 30%
checks.value: running median 0.5 d: 22.9 ppt (SNR 6.3); running median 1 d: 25.3 ppt (SNR 5.6); running median 2 d: 26 ppt (SNR 5.2); local quadratic 1.5 d: 25.5 ppt (SNR 4.9)

checks.name: Depth stability
checks.detail: one transit: nothing to compare its depth with (the pipeline and detrending checks test it instead)

checks.name: Odd/even depths
checks.detail: one transit: there are no alternate transits to compare

checks.name: Secondary eclipse
checks.detail: another significant dip at BTJD 3735.01 (43% of the depth): a secondary eclipse of a binary, or a second transit
checks.value: deepest other dip: BTJD 3735.01, 10.9 ppt (6.3σ red); limit for an eclipse anywhere in 342 d of data: 4.25 ppt (3σ red)

checks.name: Transit shape
checks.detail: the trapezoid fit didn't converge

checks.name: Duration vs expected
checks.detail: with no period, the duration bounds it instead: P ≳ 5.3 d on this star (central, circular orbit)

checks.name: Period from the transit shape
checks.detail: no shape fit

checks.name: Variability at the transit period
checks.detail: no variability above 0.5 ppt out of transit (smaller pulsations are handled by the pulsation test)

checks.name: Pulsation removal
checks.detail: the transit survives subtracting the star's pulsations, at the same depth
checks.value: 1 periodic signal removed: 8.16 h (4.87 ppt); transit 25.3 ppt (SNR 5.6) → 25.7 ppt (SNR 6.2), 8 sectors

checks.name: Archival radial velocities
checks.detail: no archival RVs: Gaia DR3 has no RV time series for the star (too faint or too hot for RVS); not in APOGEE DR17

checks.name: Centroid shift
checks.detail: no significant centroid motion: the source is within ~5″ of the target (3σ)

checks.name: Difference imaging
checks.detail: ran on 1 sector, but no source visible in the pixels (1.5σ): the transit is too shallow for TESS's full-frame images; it can't say which star dims

checks.name: Aperture dependence
checks.detail: large/small depth ratio 3.11 (4.2σ). Not scored: QLP's 1x1 and 5x5 px apertures aren't dilution-corrected, and known on-target planets differ by up to 3x too; a pixel-level (TPF) test is needed

checks.name: Nearby sources
checks.detail: 1 star within 1′ (3 TESS pixels) could make the dip and the pixel and centroid tests rule out the other 12: needs seeing-limited photometry of the neighbours on a transit night
checks.value: 13 of 84 Gaia DR3 stars within 2′ could cause a 25.3 ppt dip if eclipsed: Gaia 5261603944288760576 at 2″, T 13.6 (needs a 5% eclipse); Gaia 5261604013008237056 at 13″, T 15.9 (needs a 28% eclipse); Gaia 5261604730267280000 at 52″, T 17.3 (needs a 91% eclipse); Gaia 5261604734562740736 at 56″, T 16.5 (needs a 46% eclipse)

checks.name: Unresolved companions
checks.detail: Gaia sees no companion beyond ~1″ (86 au at 86 pc); closer than ~0.5-1″ (43 au at 86 pc) only speckle/AO imaging can look (the statistical validation below allows for them)

checks.name: Ground photometry (ZTF archive)
checks.detail: folds ZTF on an ephemeris: none yet without a period

checks.name: Saturation
checks.detail: too faint to saturate

checks.name: Crowding
checks.detail: 10% of the light is from other stars

checks.name: Independent pipelines
checks.detail: no sector with a transit has a second pipeline's light curve

checks.name: Another season
checks.detail: a single transit can only be in one season

checks.name: False-positive probability
checks.detail: no transit shape

checks.name: High-resolution imaging
checks.detail: speckle or AO imaging to find companions at 0.05-2″ (none on ExoFOP yet)

checks.name: Ground photometry
checks.detail: deep enough for 0.4-1 m telescopes; no ephemeris yet (one transit): it needs more TESS data first

checks.name: Reconnaissance RVs
checks.detail: a 0.08 M☉ companion at P ≥ 8.04 d would give K ≈ 15.9 km/s: a few spectra at ~100 m/s rule out a stellar companion and show double lines

checks.name: Precision RVs
checks.detail: K ≈ 20.8 m/s for ~34.7 M⊕ (mass from radius, Chen & Kipping 2017); faint for precision RVs
